remote.title: Remote Testbench
remote.intro: Start the machine that owns the browsers and devices with browser-testbench start --remote. Start the development computer normally, then use Discover on the Overview page. The first connection asks for the six-digit code shown by the remote computer; later explicit connections reuse the saved pairing.
remote.network: If discovery is blocked, use browser-testbench connect --server http://HOST:55808. A remote browser cannot reach an application through the development computer's localhost address. Bind the application to the LAN and use its explicit LAN URL. Remote mode uses unencrypted HTTP: pairing authenticates requests but does not encrypt test input, diagnostics, screenshots, or artifacts. Use it only on a trusted private network. For other networks, place a TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of a loopback Testbench and set its upstream Host header to 127.0.0.1 or localhost.

ios.title: Connect a physical iPhone or iPad
ios.showGuide: Show full iPhone and iPad setup guide
ios.toolsTitle: Install Xcode and the iOS test tools
ios.tools1: Install and open Xcode on the Mac that runs Browser Testbench.
ios.tools2: Under Xcode Settings → Accounts, add a free Apple Account or an account belonging to a paid Apple Developer team. Browser Testbench never asks for or stores the account credentials.
ios.tools3After: if Browser Testbench offers that action.
ios.device1: Connect the unlocked iPhone or iPad by USB and accept Trust This Computer.
ios.device2: Under Settings → Privacy & Security, enable Developer Mode, restart the device, and confirm it after the restart.
ios.device3: In Xcode, open Window → Devices and Simulators, select the device, and wait until it appears without a warning or a Preparing status.
ios.safari1: Under Settings → Developer, enable UI Automation.
ios.safari2: Under Settings → Safari → Advanced on iOS 16, or Settings → Apps → Safari → Advanced on newer iOS versions, enable Web Inspector and Remote Automation.
ios.signingIntro: Appium controls a real iPhone through WebDriverAgent. Apple requires this helper app to have an Apple Development certificate and a provisioning profile. A free Apple Account is sufficient.
ios.identity1After: run the WebDriverAgent command shown for the iPhone. Keep the opened WebDriverAgent.xcodeproj project open.
ios.identity2: In Xcode Settings → Accounts, select the team, open Manage Certificates, and create an Apple Development certificate if none exists.
ios.identity3: Return to the Overview page, select Check again, and copy the exact WebDriverAgent bundle ID shown for the device.
ios.teamId: If more than one team is installed, set BROWSER_TESTBENCH_IOS_TEAM_ID to the intended ten-character team ID and restart Browser Testbench.
ios.certificateTitle: If the certificate is not detected
ios.certificate1: In Keychain Access, select login → My Certificates and expand Apple Development. A private key must appear below it.
ios.certificate2Before: If the identity remains invalid, install Apple's
ios.certificate2After: in the login keychain and keep Use System Defaults.
ios.run1: A paid Developer team can first run the physical target and let Xcode provision automatically.
ios.run2: For a Personal Team or failed automatic provisioning, select WebDriverAgentRunner → Signing & Capabilities, enable automatic signing, select the team, and enter the bundle ID shown by Browser Testbench.
ios.run3: Select Product → Scheme → WebDriverAgentRunner, select the iPhone under Product → Destination, and choose Product → Test.
ios.run4: If iOS blocks the app, open Settings → General → VPN & Device Management, select the developer entry, and trust it. The device needs internet access for this confirmation.
ios.run5After: and run the physical iPhone target again.
ios.expiry: A free Personal Team profile expires after seven days. Repeat Product → Test after expiry or when an XCUITest update replaces WebDriverAgent.
ios.compatIntro: If the build succeeds but Xcode cannot start WebDriverAgentRunner, signing is already complete. Xcode 26.4 and 26.6 are known to report this error for physical iOS 16 devices.
ios.compat2: Extract it, rename it to Xcode-26.2.app, and move it to Applications.
ios.compat3: Select it and verify the version:
ios.compat4: Under Xcode Settings → Components, install the iOS 26.2 platform component if Xcode offers it.
ios.compat5: Return to Test targets and run the physical iPhone target again.
ios.networkIntro: The device needs network access to the tested application, not to the Testbench UI. USB is used separately for device discovery and automation. On the device, localhost refers to the device itself.
ios.networkRemote: You must use the IP address of the Testbench that runs the tests. Do not use the IP address of the local gateway.
ios.networkLocal: The current Testbench's detected LAN address is {address}. For an application on port 3000, you must use http://{address}:3000 instead of http://localhost:3000.
ios.networkMissing: Browser Testbench could not detect a LAN address for this computer. Check its network settings before connecting the device.
